name: Computer Science Fundamentals
tagline: Understand how computers and software really work.
description: The core of a computer science degree, minus the filler: number systems and logic, how a CPU runs code, operating systems, data structures, algorithms and their complexity, networking, security and the math that ties it together.
outcome: You can explain what happens from source code to running program, reason about performance, and pick sound data structures and algorithms.

stages.title: The machine
stages.summary: Bits, logic, number systems and how a CPU executes instructions.
stages.milestone: Trace a program from source to machine instructions and memory.

stages.title: Systems
stages.summary: Operating systems, networks and the basics of building larger systems.
stages.milestone: Explain processes, memory, the network stack and a client-server system.

stages.title: Data structures and algorithms
stages.summary: Complexity, the essential structures and the classic algorithms.
stages.milestone: Analyze code with Big-O and choose structures to match the access pattern.

stages.title: Math for computing
stages.summary: Probability, linear algebra and calculus as used in CS.
stages.milestone: Use probability and vectors to reason about algorithms and data.

stages.title: Security
stages.summary: Threats, defenses and the cryptography underneath secure systems.
stages.milestone: Explain how TLS protects a web request and where systems usually fail.
